newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan vegoil imports likely to fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan vegoil imports likely to fall sharply.

text.p: Pakistan's vegetable oil imports are likely to fall sharply due to the devaluation of the rupee and a bumper cottonseed crop, analysts said on Thursday.

"We expect about five percent lower imports of palm oil due to the devaluation of the rupee and another 10 percent decline owing to a bumper cottonseed crop," a Pakistan Vanaspati Manufacturers Association official said.

The official, who asked not to be named, said the devaluation of the rupee by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan by 3.79 percent, adjusting the rupee to 36.9700/37.1549 to the dollar on Tuesday from 35.6200/35.7981 fixed on August 29 would be a key reason for lower imports.
The rupee has fallen 5.31 percent since the financial year began on July 1, 1996, when the official conversion rate was 35.1000/35.2755 to the dollar, one foreign banker said.
Pakistan's vegoil imports fell 18.04 percent to 1.142 million tonnes worth $855.129 million in 1995/96 (July-June), compared to 1.394 million tonnes worth $997.251 million in 1994/95.

Imports of palm oil fell 14.72 percent to 0.984 million tonnes in 1995/96 from 1.154 million tonnes in 1994/95 and soyoil plunged 34 percent to 0.158 million tonnes from 0.240 million tonnes respectively.

"Vegetable oil imports including palm oil and soyoil are likely to fall 15 percent in 1996/97 due to the devaluation and an expected bumper crop of cottonseed," dealer Saulat Khan of Saulat Enterprises said.
"The devaluation will have a negative effect on the imports of palm oil and soyoil," Khan said.

Another factor for the sharp fall was an expected cotton crop of 11 million 375-lb bales, which would provide some 550,000 tonnes of cottonseed oil in 1996/97, compared to 450,000 tonnes in 1995/96, Khan said.
Pakistan produced 9.94 million cotton bales in 1995/96.

One official of the state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said: "Vegetable oil consumption is likely to fall after the devaluation which increased the prices of palm oil produced by private vegetable oil processing units."
"We have to pay more in rupees to finance the palmoil import bill in the dollars," the TCP official said.

Rashid Jan Mohammad, an importer of palm oil, said palmoil imports would slow down in the next few months due to higher stocks of the commodity in local markets and an expected availability of cottonseed oil from the 1996/97 cotton crop.
"The imports are likely to fall due to higher prices on the international markets, the rupee's devaluation and availability of locally-produced oils," Jan Mohammad said.
